title: menelausRatio: the signed division ratio of a transversal hyperplane
content: For a hyperplane with nonzero vertex values a, menelausRatio a i j is defined as -a_i / a_j. This is the signed ratio in which the hyperplane divides the edge from vertex i to vertex j: the point (1-t)V_i + tV_j with ℓ = c sits at t = a_i/(a_i - a_j), so the signed division ratio t/(1-t) = -a_i/a_j. The single extra minus sign per edge (compared to the parent's positive edge ratio) is the entire difference between Menelaus and Ceva.

title: menelausRatio_twisted_cocycle: the signed (twisted) cocycle law
content: Chaining two signed ratios introduces exactly one sign: m(i,j)·m(j,k) = -m(i,k). This is the Menelaus analogue of the parent's Ceva cocycle r(i,j)·r(j,k) = r(i,k). The twist (the extra minus) is what turns 2-face products from +1 into -1, distinguishing a transversal hyperplane from a concurrency point.

title: menelausRatio_triangle: the Menelaus product -1 on every 2-face
content: Around any triangle i → j → k → i of the simplex the product of signed ratios is -1. For the planar triangle this is precisely the classical Menelaus criterion that the three division points are collinear (lie on a transversal line). This is the headline collinearity statement, holding on every triangular 2-face of an n-simplex.

title: menelausRatio_cycle_prod: closed-walk product equals (-1)^L
content: For the signed ratios of a transversal hyperplane, the product around any closed walk v_0 → v_1 → ⋯ → v_L = v_0 equals (-1)^L. Writing m(i,j) = (-1)·(a_i/a_j) and telescoping the a-ratios to 1 leaves only the sign factor. Odd cycles (triangles, L = 3) give -1; even cycles return to +1 — the tetrahedron's 4-vertex loop is the simplest example.

title: exists_values_of_twisted_cocycle: reconstructing the hyperplane
content: The substantive converse: any nonzero signed assignment obeying the twisted cocycle law m(i,j)·m(j,k) = -m(i,k) comes from vertex values, with a_i = 1/m(b,i) for any base vertex b. The twisted cocycle m(b,i)·m(i,j) = -m(b,j) is exactly the statement m(i,j) = -a_i/a_j. So realizability by a transversal hyperplane is precisely the twisted-coboundary condition.

title: twisted_cocycle_iff_triangles / menelaus_criterion: the equivalence
content: For nonzero m the twisted cocycle law is equivalent to the Menelaus product = -1 on every ordered triple, hence a transversal hyperplane realizing m exists iff the Menelaus equation holds on every triangular 2-face. The only nonlinear step is cube_eq_neg_one: over ℝ the cube relation m(i,i)³ = -1 forces m(i,i) = -1 (the factor x²-x+1 is positive), which then yields signed reciprocity and the twisted cocycle by cancellation.
mathContext: (\forall i j k,\; m(i,j)m(j,k) = -m(i,k)) \iff (\forall i j k,\; m(i,j)m(j,k)m(k,i) = -1)

title: menelausRatio_eq_neg_edgeRatio / menelaus_triangle_eq_neg_ceva: the sign signature
content: The signed Menelaus ratio is literally the negated parent edge ratio with reversed orientation: m(i,j) = -r(j,i). Consequently the Menelaus 2-face product is the negation of the Ceva 2-face product — -1 for a transversal hyperplane versus +1 for a concurrency point. Collinearity and concurrency are one identity up to a single sign, the cleanest possible statement of Ceva–Menelaus duality.
